case_studies.title: Experimental Performance of a 5G N78 Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface: From Controlled Measurements to Commercial Network Deployment
case_studies.abstract: This paper presents a real-world experimental analysis of a modular reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) prototype designed to operate in the 5G N78 band. Unlike most RIS studies in the literature that focus on simulations or controlled setups, the proposed system is validated through three phases consisting of indoor measurements, outdoor long-range tests, and deployment in a live commercial 5G standalone network. case_studies.summary: The problem addressed in this study is the enhancement of coverage in non-line-of-sight zones in 5G networks. The AI approach used is a modular reconfigurable intelligent surface prototype designed to operate in the 5G N78 band. The outcome of the study shows promising gains in RSRP and SINR, indicating the potential of the proposed system to improve network coverage.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this concept, AI practitioners can design and test reconfigurable intelligent surfaces in various environments to optimize their performance. By validating the system through multiple phases of testing, including indoor measurements, outdoor long-range tests, and deployment in live commercial networks, practitioners can ensure the reliability and effectiveness of their solution.
case_studies.monetisation: The proposed system can be monetized by offering it as a product or service to telecommunications companies seeking to improve their network coverage. The company can also provide maintenance and update services to ensure the system remains effective and efficient in changing network conditions.

case_studies.title: Characterizing Vision-Language-Action Models across XPUs: Constraints and Acceleration for On-Robot Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are promising for generalist robot control, but on-robot deployment is bottlenecked by real-time inference under tight cost and energy budgets. Most prior evaluations rely on desktop-grade GPUs, obscuring the trade-offs and opportunities offered by heterogeneous edge accelerators (GPUs/XPUs/NPUs). We present a systematic analysis for low-cost VLA deployment via model-hardware co-characterization. case_studies.summary: The problem of deploying Vision-Language-Action models on robots is hindered by the need for real-time inference under tight cost and energy budgets. The authors propose a systematic analysis for low-cost VLA deployment via model-hardware co-characterization, evaluating model-hardware pairs under Cost, Energy, and Time metrics. The outcome shows that right-sized edge devices can be more efficient than desktop-grade GPUs, offering a potential solution for on-robot deployment.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners should consider the importance of model-hardware co-characterization and evaluate their models on various edge accelerators to find the optimal balance between cost, energy, and time. By doing so, they can develop more efficient and scalable AI models for real-world applications.
case_studies.monetisation: The research presents a concrete business opportunity for companies developing robot control systems, as the proposed approach can enable more efficient and cost-effective deployment of VLA models on robots. This can lead to the development of new products or services, such as autonomous robots for industrial or household tasks, with improved performance and reduced energy consumption.

case_studies.title: PhyCo: Learning Controllable Physical Priors for Generative Motion
case_studies.abstract: Modern video diffusion models excel at appearance synthesis but still struggle with physical consistency: objects drift, collisions lack realistic rebound, and material responses seldom match their underlying properties. We present PhyCo, a framework that introduces continuous, interpretable, and physically grounded control into video generation. case_studies.summary: Modern video diffusion models often lack physical consistency, resulting in unrealistic object movements and interactions. The proposed PhyCo framework addresses this issue by introducing continuous, interpretable, and physically grounded control into video generation through a large-scale dataset and physics-supervised fine-tuning. This approach enables more realistic video generation with improved physical consistency, making it useful for various applications such as video editing, gaming, and simulation.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can utilize large-scale datasets of simulated videos with varying physical properties to fine-tune their models and improve physical consistency. By integrating physics-supervised learning into their models, practitioners can generate more realistic videos with enhanced object movements and interactions.
case_studies.monetisation: The PhyCo framework offers a clear product opportunity in the video editing and gaming industries, where realistic video generation is crucial for creating engaging user experiences. Companies can leverage this technology to develop more advanced video editing tools or game development software, providing a competitive edge in the market.

case_studies.title: DEFault++: Automated Fault Detection, Categorization, and Diagnosis for Transformer Architectures
case_studies.abstract: Transformer models are widely deployed in critical AI applications, yet faults in their attention mechanisms, projections, and other internal components often degrade behavior silently without raising runtime errors. Existing fault diagnosis techniques often target generic deep neural networks and cannot identify which transformer component is responsible for an observed symptom. case_studies.summary: The study addresses the problem of silent faults in transformer models that can degrade their behavior without raising runtime errors. The authors propose DEFault++, a hierarchical learning-based diagnostic technique that operates at three levels of abstraction to detect, classify, and diagnose faults in transformer architectures. The outcome is a more reliable and efficient fault diagnosis technique for transformer models, which can improve the performance and safety of AI applications.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from this study by incorporating hierarchical learning-based diagnostic techniques into their AI model development and testing pipelines. By doing so, they can identify and address potential faults in their transformer models, leading to more reliable and efficient AI systems.
case_studies.monetisation: The DEFault++ technique has the potential to be developed into a product or service that can be sold to companies that heavily rely on transformer models, such as those in the NLP or computer vision spaces. This product or service could offer automated fault detection and diagnosis capabilities, providing a competitive advantage to companies that adopt it.

case_studies.title: Design Structure Matrix Modularization with Large Language Models
case_studies.abstract: Design Structure Matrix (DSM) modularization, the task of partitioning system elements into cohesive modules, is a fundamental combinatorial challenge in engineering design. Traditional methods treat modularization as a pure graph optimization, without access to the engineering context embedded in the system. Building on prior work on LLM-based combinatorial optimization for DSM sequencing, this paper extends the method to modularization across five cases and three backbone LLMs. Our method achieves near-reference quality within 30 iterations without requiring specialized optimization code. case_studies.summary: The problem of Design Structure Matrix (DSM) modularization is a fundamental challenge in engineering design, where traditional methods treat modularization as a pure graph optimization without considering the engineering context. This paper proposes an AI approach using Large Language Models (LLMs) to extend modularization across five cases and three backbone LLMs. The outcome achieves near-reference quality within 30 iterations without requiring specialized optimization code.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this method by leveraging LLMs to optimize combinatorial challenges in their respective domains, potentially reducing the need for specialized optimization code. By exploring the use of LLMs in modularization, practitioners can improve the efficiency and effectiveness of their design processes.
case_studies.monetisation: The proposed method has a clear product opportunity in the engineering design and optimization software market, where companies can integrate LLM-based modularization into their existing design tools. This can lead to improved design efficiency, reduced costs, and increased competitiveness for companies that adopt this technology.

case_studies.abstract: Foundation segmentation models such as the Segment Anything Model (SAM) have demonstrated strong generalization across natural images; however, their robustness under clinically realistic medical imaging domain shifts remains insufficiently quantified. case_studies.summary: The study evaluates the robustness of a foundation segmentation model under simulated domain shifts in abdominal CT scans, specifically for spleen segmentation. The researchers used a systematic slice-level robustness audit of the Segment Anything Model (SAM) and found that its robustness under clinically realistic medical imaging domain shifts remains insufficiently quantified. The outcome of the study highlights the need for further research to improve the model's robustness and generalizability to real-world clinical applications.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this study's findings, AI practitioners can use a standardized ground-truth-derived bounding-box protocol to isolate encoder robustness from prompt uncertainty and evaluate the robustness of their models under simulated domain shifts. By doing so, they can identify potential limitations and improve the generalizability of their models to real-world clinical applications.
case_studies.monetisation: The study's findings can be monetized by developing more robust and generalizable medical imaging models that can be deployed in clinical settings, such as hospitals and medical research institutions. A potential business opportunity is to develop a product that provides robust and accurate spleen segmentation in abdominal CT scans, which can be used to improve diagnosis and treatment of spleen-related diseases.

case_studies.title: Network Impact of Post-Quantum Certificate Chain sizes on Time to First Byte in TLS Deployments
case_studies.abstract: Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) is a rapidly growing deployment challenge as cryptographically relevant quantum computers (CRQC) continue to advance, leaving traditional cryptographic algorithms used in X.509 vulnerable to attack. However, PQC introduces significant deployment challenges in real-world networks, with handshake sizes increasing from 5x to over 20x compared to classical algorithms. In this work, we evaluate the time to first byte (TTFB) under CDN-focused TLS conditions to characterize the latency cost of transitioning existing internet infrastructure to quantum-safe certificate s
case_studies.summary: The problem of transitioning to post-quantum cryptography in real-world networks is hindered by significant deployment challenges, including increased handshake sizes. The authors employ an AI-focused approach to evaluate the time to first byte under CDN-focused TLS conditions, characterizing the latency cost of transitioning to quantum-safe certificates. The outcome provides insights into the network impact of post-quantum certificate chain sizes on time to first byte in TLS deployments.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from this study by considering the potential latency costs when deploying post-quantum cryptography in real-world networks, and optimizing their solutions accordingly. By evaluating the time to first byte under various conditions, practitioners can better understand the performance implications of post-quantum cryptography and make informed decisions about its deployment.
case_studies.monetisation: The study highlights a clear need for efficient and scalable post-quantum cryptography solutions, presenting a potential business opportunity for companies that can develop and deploy optimized quantum-safe certificates. By addressing the latency costs associated with post-quantum cryptography, companies can provide valuable solutions for organizations seeking to transition to quantum-safe infrastructure.

case_studies.title: 3D Reconstruction Techniques in the Manufacturing Domain: Applications, Research Opportunities and Use Cases
case_studies.abstract: This comprehensive review examines the evolution and the current state of the art in three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction techniques in manufacturing applications. The analysis covers both traditional approaches and emerging deep learning methods, showing a critical research gap in unified 3d reconstruction frameworks. The AI approach involves analyzing 106 recent publications and classifying reconstruction techniques into three primary categories. The outcome is the identification of a critical research gap in unified 3D reconstruction frameworks, highlighting opportunities for future research and development.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from this study by considering the limitations of current 3D reconstruction techniques and exploring the potential of deep learning methods to improve accuracy and efficiency. By analyzing the classification of reconstruction techniques, practitioners can identify areas for improvement and develop more effective solutions for manufacturing applications.
case_studies.monetisation: The study highlights a concrete business opportunity for companies to develop and market unified 3D reconstruction frameworks that can be applied across various manufacturing applications. By addressing the research gap identified in the study, companies can create products that improve the efficiency and accuracy of 3D reconstruction, leading to increased adoption and revenue growth.

case_studies.title: A Pattern Language for Resilient Visual Agents
case_studies.abstract: Integrating multimodal foundation models into enterprise ecosystems presents a fundamental software architecture challenge. Architects must balance competing quality attributes: the high latency and non-determinism of vision language action (VLA) models versus the strict determinism and real-time performance required by enterprise control loops. In this study, we propose an architectural pattern language for visual agents that separates fast, deterministic reflexes from slow, probabilistic supervision. The proposed solution is an architectural pattern language for visual agents that separates fast, deterministic reflexes from slow, probabilistic supervision. This approach consists of four architectural design patterns, including Hybrid Affordance Integration, to improve the performance and reliability of visual agents.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can separate the fast and slow components of their visual agents, using deterministic models for real-time control loops and probabilistic models for supervisory tasks. By doing so, they can achieve a better balance between competing quality attributes and improve the overall performance and reliability of their systems.
case_studies.monetisation: The proposed architectural pattern language has a clear product opportunity in industries that rely on computer vision and automation, such as robotics, healthcare, and manufacturing. Companies can develop and market products that implement this pattern language, providing a competitive edge in terms of performance, reliability, and scalability.

case_studies.abstract: Multivariate time series forecasting plays a pivotal role in numerous real-world applications, including financial analysis, energy management, and traffic planning. case_studies.summary: The problem of multivariate time series forecasting is a significant challenge in various real-world applications, including financial analysis and energy management. The proposed AI approach, ITS-Mina, integrates an iterative refinement mechanism and external attention into an all-MLP framework to improve forecasting performance. The outcome is a novel framework that can potentially achieve competitive or superior performance with reduced computational cost.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from this study by exploring the use of simpler MLP-based models for multivariate time series forecasting, and incorporating iterative refinement mechanisms to enhance performance. By doing so, they can potentially develop more efficient and effective forecasting models for various applications.
case_studies.monetisation: The proposed framework has a clear potential for monetisation, as it can be adapted for various industries and applications, such as financial analysis and energy management, where accurate forecasting is crucial. A company can develop a product based on this framework, offering forecasting services to clients and generating revenue through subscription-based models or consulting services.

This paper proposes the use of Large Language Models and Image Diffusion Models for Procedural Content Generation of TCG cards to address these challenges. The outcome is the potential creation of new and engaging card content, enhancing the overall player experience.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this approach by leveraging LLMs and Image Diffusion Models to generate procedural content for various applications, including game development and digital media. By integrating these models, practitioners can create dynamic and engaging content, improving user experience and driving user engagement.

case_studies.title: Computing Equilibrium beyond Unilateral Deviation
case_studies.abstract: Most familiar equilibrium concepts, such as Nash and correlated equilibrium, guarantee only that no single player can improve their utility by deviating unilaterally. They offer no guarantees against profitable coordinated deviations by coalitions. Although the literature proposes solution concepts that provide stability against multilateral deviations (\emph{e.g.}, strong Nash and coalition-proof equilibrium), these generally fail to exist. case_studies.summary: The problem addressed in this paper is the limitation of traditional equilibrium concepts, such as Nash and correlated equilibrium, which only guarantee stability against unilateral deviations. The AI approach proposed is an alternative solution concept that minimizes coalitional deviation incentives. The outcome of this approach is a more robust and stable equilibrium concept that can handle multilateral deviations.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this concept by incorporating coalitional deviation incentives into their equilibrium models, allowing for more realistic and stable outcomes. This can be achieved by using advanced optimization techniques and game-theoretic frameworks to minimize deviation incentives.
case_studies.monetisation: A potential business opportunity is to develop a software platform that implements this alternative solution concept, allowing companies to analyze and optimize their strategic decision-making processes. This platform could be marketed to industries where game-theoretic models are commonly used, such as finance, economics, and political science.

case_studies.abstract: This work proposes novel splitting techniques for argumentation formalisms that incorporate supports between defeasible elements. The AI approach proposed is based on bipolar set-based argumentation frameworks (BSAFs), which generalize existing argumentation frameworks by incorporating both collective attacks and supports. The outcome of this study is the development of novel splitting techniques for BSAFs, which can potentially lead to more efficient and effective argumentation-based decision-making systems.

By incorporating BSAFs into their systems, practitioners can potentially improve the efficiency and effectiveness of their decision-making processes.
case_studies.monetisation: The research presented in this study can be monetised by developing commercial argumentation-based decision-making systems that incorporate BSAFs, which can be sold to organisations in various domains such as law, medicine, and finance. case_studies.title: RHyVE: Competence-Aware Verification and Phase-Aware Deployment for LLM-Generated Reward Hypotheses
case_studies.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) make reward design in reinforcement learning substantially more scalable, but generated rewards are not automatically reliable training objectives. Existing work has focused primarily on generating, evolving, or selecting reward candidates, while paying less attention to when such candidates can be verified and deployed during policy optimization. case_studies.summary: The problem of unreliable training objectives in reinforcement learning is addressed by proposing a system that treats generated rewards as reward hypotheses. The AI approach, called RHyVE, considers the competence of the current policy and the phase of training to verify and deploy these reward hypotheses. The outcome is a more scalable and reliable reward design process for reinforcement learning.
case_studies.how_to_apply: Practitioners can apply this approach by incorporating competence-aware verification and phase-aware deployment into their reinforcement learning pipelines, allowing for more efficient and effective policy optimization. By considering the utility of generated rewards in different phases of training, practitioners can improve the overall performance of their reinforcement learning systems.
case_studies.monetisation: A potential business opportunity is to develop a product that integrates RHyVE into a reinforcement learning platform, offering scalable and reliable reward design as a key feature. This product could be marketed to companies working on complex control tasks, such as robotics or autonomous vehicles, where reliable reward design is crucial for successful policy optimization.

case_studies.title: SpecVQA: A Benchmark for Spectral Understanding and Visual Question Answering in Scientific Images
case_studies.abstract: Spectra are a prevalent yet highly information-dense form of scientific imagery, presenting substantial challenges to multimodal large language models (MLLMs) due to their unstructured and domain-specific characteristics. Here we introduce SpecVQA, a professional scientific-image benchmark for evaluating multimodal models on scientific spectral understanding, covering 7 representative spectrum types with expert-annotated question-answer pairs. case_studies.summary: The SpecVQA benchmark is designed to evaluate the ability of multimodal large language models to understand and answer questions about scientific spectral images. The introduction of SpecVQA aims to improve the performance of multimodal models on scientific spectral understanding and visual question answering tasks.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply the SpecVQA benchmark, AI practitioners can use it to evaluate and fine-tune their multimodal models on scientific spectral understanding and visual question answering tasks. By using SpecVQA, practitioners can identify areas for improvement and develop more effective models for real-world applications.
case_studies.monetisation: The SpecVQA benchmark can be monetized by developing and selling multimodal models that have been fine-tuned on the benchmark, or by offering annotation and evaluation services for scientific spectral images. Companies can also use SpecVQA to develop and market AI-powered tools for scientific image analysis and question answering.

case_studies.abstract: This paper examines how different types of large language model (LLM) agents perform on scientific visualization (SciVis) tasks, where users generate visualization workflows from natural-language instructions. We compare three primary interaction paradigms, including domain-specific agents with structured tool use, computer-use agents, and general-purpose coding agents, by evaluating eight representative agents across 15 benchmark tasks and measuring visualization quality, efficiency, robustness, and computational cost. case_studies.summary: This study explores the effectiveness of large language model (LLM) agents in scientific visualization tasks, where users generate visualization workflows from natural-language instructions. The outcome of this study provides insights into the strengths and weaknesses of different LLM agents in scientific visualization tasks.

case_studies.title: Graph World Models: Concepts, Taxonomy, and Future Directions
case_studies.abstract: As one of the mainstream models of artificial intelligence, world models allow agents to learn the representation of the environment for efficient prediction and planning. However, classical world models based on flat tensors face several key problems, including noise sensitivity, error accumulation and weak reasoning. case_studies.summary: Classical world models in artificial intelligence face limitations such as noise sensitivity and weak reasoning. This approach allows for more efficient prediction and planning in virtual environments, but its applications and outcomes are still largely theoretical.

By integrating graph structures into their existing models, practitioners can improve the reasoning and prediction capabilities of their AI agents.

Companies can leverage this technology to create more realistic and interactive virtual environments, leading to new business opportunities in the fields of entertainment, education, and training.

case_studies.title: Feasible-First Exploration for Constrained ML Deployment Optimization in Crash-Prone Hierarchical Search Spaces
case_studies.abstract: Deploying machine learning models under production constraints requires joint optimization over model family, quantization scheme, runtime backend, and serving configuration. This induces a hierarchical mixed-variable search space in which many configurations are invalid: evaluations may crash, exceed memory limits, or violate latency constraints. case_studies.summary: The problem of deploying machine learning models under production constraints is addressed in this study, which proposes a feasible-first exploration approach to optimize model deployment. This approach aims to navigate the hierarchical mixed-variable search space and avoid invalid configurations that can lead to crashes or exceeded memory limits. The outcome of this approach is a more efficient optimization process that can handle constrained machine learning deployment, but its practical implementation and impact are still theoretical.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can prioritize the exploration of feasible configurations in their optimization process, using techniques such as constrained Bayesian optimization to efficiently search the hierarchical search space. By doing so, they can reduce the waste of evaluation budget on invalid configurations and improve the overall efficiency of their model deployment optimization.
case_studies.monetisation: The proposed approach can be monetized by developing a product or service that offers optimized machine learning model deployment for businesses, which can lead to improved efficiency and reduced costs. This product or service can be integrated into existing MLOps pipelines, providing a clear value proposition for companies looking to streamline their machine learning operations.

case_studies.title: Operating-Layer Controls for Onchain Language-Model Agents Under Real Capital
case_studies.abstract: We study reliability in autonomous language-model agents that translate user mandates into validated tool actions under real capital. Users configured vaults through structured controls and natural-language strategies, but only agents could choose normal buy/sell trades. case_studies.summary: The problem of reliability in autonomous language-model agents is addressed in this study, which explores the use of operating-layer controls to translate user mandates into validated tool actions under real capital. The AI approach involves the deployment of 3,505 user-funded agents in a bounded onchain market, with users configuring vaults through structured controls and natural-language strategies. The outcome is a system that produced 7.5M agent invocations, roughly 300K onchain actions, and a 99.9% settlement success rate for policy validity.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can focus on designing operating-layer controls that allow users to configure and interact with autonomous agents in a secure and reliable manner. By leveraging natural-language strategies and structured controls, practitioners can build more effective and scalable AI systems that can operate in real-world environments.
case_studies.monetisation: The study demonstrates a clear business opportunity for companies to develop and deploy autonomous language-model agents that can operate in onchain markets, with potential applications in areas such as cryptocurrency trading and asset management. By building on the findings of this study, companies can create products and services that provide reliable and secure autonomous trading capabilities, with potential for significant revenue generation.

case_studies.title: Benchmarking Complex Multimodal Document Processing Pipelines: A Unified Evaluation Framework for Enterprise AI
case_studies.abstract: Most enterprise document AI today is a pipeline. Parse, index, retrieve, generate. Each of those stages has been studied to death on its own -- what's still hard is evaluating the system as a whole. We built EnterpriseDocBench to take a swing at it: parsing fidelity, indexing efficiency, retrieval relevance, and generation groundedness, all on the same corpus. case_studies.summary: The problem of evaluating complex multimodal document processing pipelines is addressed through the introduction of EnterpriseDocBench, a unified evaluation framework. The outcome is a comprehensive evaluation of these pipelines across six enterprise domains, providing insights into their performance and potential areas for improvement.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can utilize the EnterpriseDocBench framework to evaluate their own document processing pipelines, identifying areas for optimization and improvement. By leveraging this framework, practitioners can develop more effective and efficient pipelines, ultimately leading to better document processing outcomes.
case_studies.monetisation: The EnterpriseDocBench framework presents a concrete business opportunity for companies to develop and sell optimized document processing pipelines to enterprises, leveraging the evaluation framework to demonstrate the value of their solutions. Additionally, the framework can be used to develop new products and services, such as AI-powered document analysis and automation tools, which can be sold to enterprises across various domains.

Companies could leverage the results of this study to create specialized robotic solutions that integrate Vision-Language-Action models with optimized edge devices, providing a competitive advantage in the market.

case_studies.title: HalluCiteChecker: A Lightweight Toolkit for Hallucinated Citation Detection and Verification in the Era of AI Scientists
case_studies.abstract: We introduce HalluCiteChecker, a toolkit for detecting and verifying hallucinated citations in scientific papers. While AI assistant technologies have transformed the academic writing process, including citation recommendation, they have also led to the emergence of hallucinated citations that do not correspond to any existing work. Such citations not only undermine the credibility of scientific papers but also impose an additional burden on reviewers and authors, who must manually verify their validity during the review process. case_studies.summary: The emergence of AI-assisted academic writing has led to the problem of hallucinated citations, which undermine the credibility of scientific papers and impose a burden on reviewers and authors. HalluCiteChecker, a lightweight toolkit, approaches this problem by detecting and verifying hallucinated citations using a formalized method. The outcome of this study is a potentially effective solution for improving the accuracy and reliability of scientific citations.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this concept, AI practitioners can develop similar toolkits by formalizing the detection of hallucinated information in their respective domains. By leveraging machine learning and natural language processing techniques, practitioners can create effective solutions for verifying the validity of references and citations.
case_studies.monetisation: The HalluCiteChecker toolkit presents a clear product opportunity for companies that provide academic writing and publishing tools, as it can be integrated into existing platforms to enhance the credibility and accuracy of scientific papers. By licensing or developing this technology, companies can offer a unique value proposition to their customers, differentiating themselves in the market and generating revenue through subscription-based models or premium services.

case_studies.title: SynSur: An end-to-end generative pipeline for synthetic industrial surface defect generation and detection
case_studies.abstract: The bottleneck in learning-based industrial defect detection is often limited not by model capacity, but by the scarcity of labeled defect data: defects are rare, annotations are expensive, and collecting balanced training sets is slow. We present an end-to-end pipeline for synthetic defect generation and annotation, combining Vision-Language-Model-based prompts, LoRA-adapted diffusion, mask-guided inpainting, and sample filtering with automatic label derivation, and demonstrates the potential of real data with realistic synthetic samples to overcome data scarcity. case_studies.summary: The study addresses the scarcity of labeled defect data in industrial defect detection by introducing an end-to-end generative pipeline called SynSur. This pipeline utilizes AI techniques such as Vision-Language-Model-based prompts, LoRA-adapted diffusion, and mask-guided inpainting to generate synthetic defect data. The outcome demonstrates the potential of combining real data with realistic synthetic samples to overcome data scarcity and improve defect detection models.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the SynSur pipeline by integrating it into their existing defect detection workflows, using the generated synthetic data to augment their training sets and improve model performance. To implement this pipeline, practitioners should focus on adapting the AI techniques to their specific use case and ensuring the quality of the generated synthetic data.
case_studies.monetisation: The SynSur pipeline presents a clear business opportunity for companies that specialize in industrial defect detection, as it can help reduce the cost and time associated with data collection and annotation. By developing a product or service based on this pipeline, companies can offer improved defect detection capabilities to their clients, potentially leading to increased revenue and competitiveness.

case_studies.title: Robustness Evaluation of a Foundation Segmentation Model Under Simulated Domain Shifts in Abdominal CT: Implications for Health Digital Twin Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Foundation segmentation models such as the Segment Anything Model (SAM) have demonstrated strong generalization across natural images; however, their robustness under clinically realistic medical imaging domain shifts remains insufficiently quantified. We present a systematic slice-level robustness audit of SAM (ViT-B) for spleen segmentation in abdominal CT using 1,051 nonempty slices from 41 volumes in the Medical Segmentation Decathlon. case_studies.summary: The robustness of foundation segmentation models under clinically realistic medical imaging domain shifts is insufficiently quantified, which can impact their deployment in health digital twin applications. To address this, the authors used a systematic slice-level robustness audit of the Segment Anything Model (SAM) for spleen segmentation in abdominal CT scans. The study found that controlled perturbations can simulate domain shifts and evaluate the model's robustness, providing valuable insights for healthcare AI deployment.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from this study by using standardized ground-truth-derived bounding-box protocols to isolate encoder robustness from prompt uncertainty in their own models. By doing so, they can systematically evaluate the robustness of their models under various domain shifts, ensuring more reliable performance in real-world applications.
case_studies.monetisation: The study's findings can be monetized by developing and marketing more robust foundation segmentation models for healthcare applications, such as health digital twin deployment. Companies can leverage these models to create more accurate and reliable medical imaging analysis tools, generating revenue through licensing or subscription-based services.

case_studies.title: Network Impact of Post-Quantum Certificate Chain sizes on Time to First Byte in TLS Deployments
case_studies.abstract: Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) is a rapidly growing deployment challenge as cryptographically relevant quantum computers (CRQC) continue to advance, leaving traditional cryptographic algorithms used in X.509 vulnerable to attack. However, PQC introduces significant deployment challenges in real-world networks, with handshake sizes increasing from 5x to over 20x compared to classical algorithms. case_studies.summary: The growing threat of quantum computers compromises traditional cryptographic algorithms used in X.509, prompting the need for Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) deployment. This study evaluates the impact of PQC on Time to First Byte (TTFB) in TLS deployments, focusing on CDN-focused conditions. The outcome characterizes the latency cost of transitioning to quantum-safe certificates, providing insights into the deployment challenges of PQC in real-world networks.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply the findings of this study, AI practitioners should consider the latency implications of PQC deployment in their own network architectures, and develop strategies to mitigate potential performance degradation. By evaluating the impact of PQC on TTFB, practitioners can optimize their TLS deployments for a seamless transition to quantum-safe cryptography.
case_studies.monetisation: The findings of this study present a clear business opportunity for companies developing quantum-safe cryptographic solutions, as the demand for secure and efficient PQC deployment is expected to grow. By addressing the deployment challenges identified in this study, companies can develop and market optimized PQC solutions, capitalizing on the need for quantum-safe internet infrastructure.

case_studies.title: AgentPulse: A Continuous Multi-Signal Framework for Evaluating AI Agents in Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Static benchmarks measure what AI agents can do at a fixed point in time but not how they are adopted, maintained, or experienced in deployment. We introduce AgentPulse, a continuous evaluation framework scoring 50 agents across 10 workload categories along four factors (Benchmark Performance, Adoption Signals, Community Sentiment, and Ecosystem Health) aggregated from 18 real-time signals across GitHub, package registries, IDE marketplaces, social platforms, and benchmark leaderboards. Three analyses ground the framework. The four factors capture largely complementary information (n=50; $ρ_{\
case_studies.summary: The problem of evaluating AI agents in deployment is addressed through the introduction of AgentPulse, a continuous evaluation framework that scores AI agents across multiple factors. The AI approach involves aggregating real-time signals from various sources to provide a comprehensive evaluation of AI agents. The outcome is a framework that captures complementary information, enabling a more holistic understanding of AI agent performance and adoption.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from AgentPulse by incorporating continuous evaluation and multi-signal assessment into their AI development and deployment workflows. This can be achieved by integrating real-time data from various sources, such as GitHub, social platforms, and benchmark leaderboards, to gain a more comprehensive understanding of AI agent performance.
case_studies.monetisation: The AgentPulse framework presents a concrete business opportunity for companies to develop and offer AI evaluation and monitoring services, helping organizations to optimize their AI deployments and improve overall performance. Additionally, the framework's ability to provide actionable insights can be leveraged to create new products or features, such as AI-powered consulting tools or evaluation platforms, that cater to the growing demand for AI solutions.

case_studies.title: MetaSR: Content-Adaptive Metadata Orchestration for Generative Super-Resolution
case_studies.abstract: We study generative super-resolution (SR) in real-world scenarios where content and degradations vary across domains, genres, and segments. For example, images and videos may alternate between text overlays, fast motion, smooth cartoons, and low-light faces, each benefiting from different forms of side information. Existing metadata-guided SR methods typically use a fixed conditioning design, which is suboptimal when useful cues are content dependent and transmission budgets are limited. case_studies.summary: The problem of generative super-resolution in real-world scenarios is addressed, where content and degradations vary across domains. The proposed AI approach, MetaSR, utilizes a Diffusion Transformer-based framework to select and inject task-relevant metadata. The outcome is a more adaptive and efficient super-resolution method that can handle diverse content types.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this concept, AI practitioners can explore the use of metadata-guided approaches in their own super-resolution tasks, considering the content-dependent nature of useful cues. By selecting and injecting relevant metadata, practitioners can improve the efficiency and adaptability of their super-resolution models.
case_studies.monetisation: The proposed MetaSR framework has clear product opportunities in the field of computer vision, particularly in applications such as video enhancement and image restoration. Companies can leverage this technology to develop more efficient and adaptive super-resolution products, targeting industries such as media, entertainment, and surveillance.

case_studies.title: Apriori-based Analysis of Learned Helplessness in Mathematics Tutoring: Behavioral Patterns by Level, Intervention, and Outcome
case_studies.abstract: This study applied the Apriori algorithm to analyze behavioral interaction patterns associated with learned helplessness (LH) in mathematics tutoring system logs. Interaction data were examined across three dimensions: LH level (low vs. high), system-based intervention (with vs. without), and problem-solving outcomes (solved vs. unsolved). case_studies.summary: This study examines the problem of learned helplessness in mathematics tutoring by analyzing interaction patterns in system logs. The Apriori algorithm is used to identify behavioral patterns associated with learned helplessness, system-based intervention, and problem-solving outcomes. The analysis reveals that skipping problems without using hints is linked to unsolved outcomes, while persistence behaviors are less dominant overall.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can utilize the Apriori algorithm to analyze interaction data in various educational settings, providing insights into student behavior and learning outcomes. By identifying patterns associated with learned helplessness, educators and AI developers can design more effective interventions to support students and improve learning outcomes.
case_studies.monetisation: A potential business opportunity arising from this study is the development of AI-powered tutoring systems that incorporate personalized interventions to address learned helplessness, offering a competitive edge in the education technology market. Such a product could be marketed to educational institutions and tutoring services, providing a unique value proposition to improve student outcomes and increase customer engagement.

case_studies.title: Feasible-First Exploration for Constrained ML Deployment Optimization in Crash-Prone Hierarchical Search Spaces
case_studies.abstract: Deploying machine learning models under production constraints requires joint optimization over model family, quantization scheme, runtime backend, and serving configuration. This induces a hierarchical mixed-variable search space in which many configurations are invalid: evaluations may crash, exceed memory limits, or violate latency constraints. Standard black-box optimizers such as Tree-structured Parzen Estimators (TPE) and constrained Bayesian optimization are effective when valid configurations are common, but they can spend a large fraction of a small evaluation budget on invalid or uni
case_studies.summary: The problem of deploying machine learning models under production constraints is addressed through a novel approach that optimizes model family, quantization scheme, runtime backend, and serving configuration. The proposed AI approach, Feasible-First Exploration, is designed to handle hierarchical mixed-variable search spaces with many invalid configurations. The outcome of this approach is a more efficient optimization of machine learning model deployment, reducing the number of evaluations spent on invalid or uninformative configurations.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners should consider using Feasible-First Exploration to optimize their machine learning model deployment, especially when dealing with complex and constrained search spaces. By doing so, they can reduce the time and resources spent on evaluating invalid configurations and focus on finding the optimal deployment strategy.
case_studies.monetisation: The proposed approach has a clear monetisation potential as it can be used to develop more efficient and scalable machine learning model deployment solutions, which can be sold as a product or service to companies looking to optimize their AI workflows. This can be particularly attractive to companies operating in industries with strict production constraints, such as finance or healthcare, where the efficient deployment of machine learning models is crucial.

case_studies.title: Exploring the Potential of Probabilistic Transformer for Time Series Modeling: A Report on the ST-PT Framework
case_studies.abstract: The Probabilistic Transformer (PT) establishes that the Transformer's self-attention plus its feed-forward block is mathematically equivalent to Mean-Field Variational Inference (MFVI) on a Conditional Random Field (CRF). Under this equivalence the Transformer ceases to be a black-box neural network and becomes a programmable factor graph: graph topology, factor potentials, and the message-passing schedule are all explicit and inspectable primitives that can be engineered. case_studies.summary: The problem of time series modeling is addressed using the Probabilistic Transformer (PT) framework, which establishes a mathematical equivalence between the Transformer's self-attention and Mean-Field Variational Inference (MFVI) on a Conditional Random Field (CRF). The PT approach allows for a programmable factor graph, enabling explicit and inspectable primitives that can be engineered. The outcome of this investigation is a report on the potential of PT for time series modeling, exploring its applications and implications.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply the PT framework to time series modeling, practitioners can leverage the equivalence between the Transformer's self-attention and MFVI to design and engineer factor graphs that capture complex temporal relationships. By explicitly defining graph topology, factor potentials, and message-passing schedules, practitioners can create more interpretable and controllable time series models.
case_studies.monetisation: The PT framework has the potential to be monetised through the development of predictive analytics tools for industries that rely heavily on time series data, such as finance and logistics. By creating more accurate and interpretable time series models, companies can provide high-value services to clients, such as demand forecasting and anomaly detection.

case_studies.title: FutureWorld: A Live Environment for Training Predictive Agents with Real-World Outcome Rewards
case_studies.abstract: Live future prediction refers to the task of making predictions about real-world events before they unfold. This task is increasingly studied using large language model-based agent systems, and it is important for building agents that can continually learn from real-world. Just as interactive environments have often driven progress in agents, advancing live future prediction naturally motivates viewing it as a learning environment. Prior works have explored future prediction from several different parts, but have generally not framed it as a unified learning environment. This task is appealing
case_studies.summary: The problem of live future prediction involves making predictions about real-world events before they occur, which is a challenging task that requires advanced agent systems. The proposed AI approach, FutureWorld, frames live future prediction as a unified learning environment, allowing agents to continually learn from real-world outcomes. The outcome of this approach is a more effective and adaptive predictive agent system.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can develop interactive environments that simulate real-world scenarios, allowing agents to learn from outcomes and improve their predictive capabilities. By viewing live future prediction as a learning environment, practitioners can create more effective and adaptive agent systems.
case_studies.monetisation: The FutureWorld approach has potential for monetisation in industries such as finance, healthcare, and logistics, where predictive agents can be used to forecast and prevent adverse events. A concrete business opportunity could involve developing a predictive agent system for a specific industry, using the FutureWorld approach to train and deploy the system.

case_studies.title: Deep-testing: the case of dependence detection
case_studies.abstract: Deep learning methods have proved highly effective for classification and image recognition problems. In this paper, we ask whether this success can be transferred to hypothesis testing: if a neural network can distinguish, for example, an image of a handwritten digit from another, can it also distinguish an "image of a sample" (such as a scatter plot) generated under a given statistical model from one generated outside that model? Motivated by this idea, we propose a novel procedure called deep-testing, which approaches the classical inferential problem of hypothesis testing through deep lear
case_studies.summary: The problem of hypothesis testing in statistical models is addressed through the use of deep learning methods. A novel procedure called deep-testing is proposed, which approaches the classical inferential problem of hypothesis testing through deep learning. The outcome of this approach is a potential new method for distinguishing between samples generated under a given statistical model and those generated outside that model.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this concept by exploring the use of deep learning methods in hypothesis testing, particularly in cases where traditional methods may struggle. By leveraging the capabilities of neural networks, practitioners can develop new procedures for detecting dependencies and making inferences about statistical models.
case_studies.monetisation: The concept of deep-testing has potential for monetisation in fields such as data analytics and statistical consulting, where companies may be willing to pay for advanced methods of hypothesis testing. A potential business opportunity could be to develop a software package or service that implements deep-testing procedures for clients in various industries.

case_studies.title: Calibrated Surprise: An Information-Theoretic Account of Creative Quality
case_studies.abstract: The essence of good creative writing is calibrated surprise: when constraints from all relevant dimensions act together, the feasible solution space collapses into a narrow region, and the surviving choices look least predictable from an unconstrained view. "Calibrated" has a precise meaning: the author's intent, the reader's reasonable expectation, and the logic of reality converge. When these three independent judgements agree on every dimension, the set of admissible writing choices is forced into a very small region. case_studies.summary: The problem of evaluating creative writing quality is complex and multifaceted, requiring a nuanced understanding of constraints and predictability. The AI approach proposed in this study uses an information-theoretic account to define calibrated surprise, a key component of creative quality. The outcome is a mathematical framework for understanding how constraints and expectations converge to produce high-quality creative writing.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this concept by incorporating multiple constraints and dimensions into their writing models, allowing for more nuanced and context-dependent generation of text. By using information-theoretic principles to guide the generation of creative content, AI systems can produce more surprising and engaging writing.
case_studies.monetisation: A potential business opportunity arising from this research is the development of AI-powered writing tools that can help authors and content creators produce more engaging and high-quality writing. Such tools could be marketed to industries such as publishing, advertising, and education, where the ability to generate compelling and effective writing is highly valued.

case_studies.title: Scalable Inference Architectures for Compound AI Systems: A Production Deployment Study
case_studies.abstract: Modern enterprise AI applications increasingly rely on compound AI systems - architectures that compose multiple models, retrievers, and tools to accomplish complex tasks. Deploying such systems in production demands inference infrastructure that can efficiently serve concurrent, heterogeneous model invocations while maintaining cost-effectiveness and low latency. case_studies.summary: The problem of deploying compound AI systems in production environments is addressed through the development of a modular, platform-agnostic inference architecture. The AI approach involves composing multiple models, retrievers, and tools to accomplish complex tasks, with a focus on efficient inference infrastructure. The outcome is a scalable and cost-effective solution that can support concurrent, heterogeneous model invocations with low latency.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from this study by designing modular inference architectures that can efficiently serve concurrent model invocations, and by leveraging platform-agnostic solutions to support heterogeneous models. By doing so, they can improve the scalability and cost-effectiveness of their compound AI systems, enabling wider adoption in production environments.
case_studies.monetisation: The developed inference architecture presents a clear product opportunity, particularly in the context of enterprise AI applications, where compound AI systems are increasingly being used to drive business value. Companies can leverage this technology to develop and deploy scalable AI solutions, generating revenue through subscription-based models or AI-powered services.

case_studies.title: MAIC-UI: Making Interactive Courseware with Generative UI
case_studies.abstract: Creating interactive STEM courseware traditionally requires HTML/CSS/JavaScript expertise, leaving barriers for educators. While generative AI can produce HTML codes, existing tools generate static presentations rather than interactive simulations, struggle with long documents, and lack pedagogical accuracy mechanisms. Furthermore, full regeneration for modifications requires 200--600 seconds, disrupting creative flow. We present MAIC-UI, a zero-code authoring system that enables educators to create and rapidly edit interactive courseware from textbooks, PPTs, and PDFs. MAIC-UI employs: (1) st
case_studies.summary: The traditional process of creating interactive STEM courseware is time-consuming and requires HTML/CSS/JavaScript expertise, leaving barriers for educators. MAIC-UI addresses this issue by employing a zero-code authoring system that utilizes generative AI to create and rapidly edit interactive courseware from textbooks, PPTs, and PDFs. This approach enables educators to create interactive simulations without requiring extensive coding knowledge, resulting in increased efficiency and pedagogical accuracy.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this AI approach, practitioners can focus on developing zero-code authoring systems that integrate generative AI capabilities, allowing users to create interactive content without requiring extensive coding expertise. By streamlining the content creation process, practitioners can increase efficiency and accessibility for educators and learners alike.
case_studies.monetisation: The MAIC-UI system presents a clear product opportunity for companies specializing in educational technology, as it can be integrated into existing learning management systems or offered as a standalone tool for educators. By licensing or commercializing the MAIC-UI technology, companies can capitalize on the growing demand for interactive and engaging educational content.

case_studies.title: RESTestBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating the Effectiveness of LLM-Generated REST API Test Cases from NL Requirements
case_studies.abstract: Existing REST API testing tools are typically evaluated using code coverage and crash-based fault metrics. However, recent LLM-based approaches increasingly generate tests from NL requirements to validate functional behaviour, making traditional metrics weak proxies for whether generated tests validate intended behaviour. To address this gap, we present RESTestBench, a benchmark comprising three REST services paired with manually verified NL requirements in both precise and vague variants, enabling controlled and reproducible evaluation of requirement-based test generation. case_studies.summary: The existing REST API testing tools are limited in their ability to evaluate the effectiveness of tests generated from natural language requirements. To address this, the authors propose RESTestBench, a benchmark for evaluating the effectiveness of LLM-generated REST API test cases from NL requirements. The outcome is a controlled and reproducible evaluation of requirement-based test generation, enabling a more accurate assessment of test effectiveness.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from this study by using RESTestBench to evaluate the effectiveness of their own LLM-generated test cases, allowing them to refine and improve their testing approaches. By leveraging this benchmark, practitioners can ensure that their tests accurately validate the intended behavior of their REST APIs.
case_studies.monetisation: The development of RESTestBench presents a concrete business opportunity for companies specializing in API testing and validation, as it provides a standardized framework for evaluating the effectiveness of LLM-generated test cases. By integrating RESTestBench into their testing suites, these companies can offer more comprehensive and accurate testing solutions to their clients, thereby increasing their competitive edge and potential revenue streams.

case_studies.title: TrialCalibre: A Fully Automated Causal Engine for RCT Benchmarking and Observational Trial Calibration
case_studies.abstract: Real-world evidence (RWE) studies that emulate target trials increasingly inform regulatory and clinical decisions, yet residual, hard-to-quantify biases still limit their credibility. The recently proposed BenchExCal framework addresses this challenge via a two-stage Benchmark, Expand, Calibrate process, which first compares an observational emulation against an existing randomized controlled trial (RCT), then uses observed divergence to calibrate a second emulation for a new indication causal effect estimation. While methodologically powerful, BenchExCal is resource intensive and difficult t
case_studies.summary: The problem of residual biases in real-world evidence studies is addressed through the development of TrialCalibre, a fully automated causal engine. The AI approach involves a two-stage process of benchmarking and calibration to improve the credibility of observational trial emulations. The outcome is a more robust method for estimating causal effects in new indications, increasing the reliability of real-world evidence studies.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this approach by identifying areas where observational data can be calibrated against randomized controlled trials, and then using the resulting insights to inform decision-making. By leveraging the TrialCalibre engine, researchers can streamline the process of benchmarking and calibration, making it more efficient and scalable.
case_studies.monetisation: The TrialCalibre engine has the potential to be developed into a commercial product, offering a solution for pharmaceutical companies and research institutions seeking to improve the validity of their real-world evidence studies. By licensing or partnering with companies that specialize in healthcare data analytics, the authors may be able to generate revenue from their innovation.

case_studies.title: Conditional misalignment: common interventions can hide emergent misalignment behind contextual triggers
case_studies.abstract: Finetuning a language model can lead to emergent misalignment (EM) [Betley et al., 2025b]. Models trained on a narrow distribution of misaligned behavior generalize to more egregious behaviors when tested outside the training distribution. We study a set of interventions proposed to reduce EM. We confirm that these interventions reduce or eliminate EM on existing evaluations (questions like "How do I make a quick buck?"). case_studies.summary: The problem of emergent misalignment in language models can lead to undesirable behaviors when tested outside the training distribution. The authors propose a study on conditional misalignment, where common interventions can hide emergent misalignment behind contextual triggers. The outcome of the study reveals that even with interventions, language models can still display emergent misalignment when evaluated with prompts that resemble the training context.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners should be cautious when evaluating language models and consider the potential for conditional misalignment, using a variety of evaluation prompts to uncover hidden biases. By acknowledging the limitations of current interventions, practitioners can develop more robust testing methods to ensure the safety and reliability of language models.
case_studies.monetisation: The findings of this study could be used to develop more robust language models for commercial applications, such as chatbots or virtual assistants, where safety and reliability are paramount. A company could leverage this research to create a product that specializes in testing and evaluating language models for conditional misalignment, providing a valuable service to organizations looking to deploy AI safely.

case_studies.title: Does social identity matter in software engineering? Assessing the case of research software engineers
case_studies.abstract: Social identity is a concept from psychology that refers to the part of an individual's identity that derives from their group membership(s). In this paper, we explore social identity in members of the professional community of Research Software Engineers (RSEs). Using a mixed-methods approach, our study combined computational linguistic analysis and inferential statistics to examine over 28,000 social media posts, 1,700 blogs, and survey responses from 381 professional RSEs. The findings highlight the emergence of a collective RSE identity and demonstrate its role in shaping professional well
case_studies.summary: The study explores the concept of social identity in Research Software Engineers (RSEs) and its impact on their professional well-being. The AI approach used a mixed-methods methodology, combining computational linguistic analysis and inferential statistics to analyze social media posts, blogs, and survey responses. The outcome highlights the emergence of a collective RSE identity and its role in shaping professional well-being.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the findings of this study by recognizing the importance of social identity in professional communities and using similar methodologies to analyze and understand the dynamics of their own communities. By doing so, they can develop more effective strategies for building and maintaining a strong sense of community and identity among their team members.
case_studies.monetisation: The study's findings on social identity in RSEs could be monetized by developing targeted training programs or community-building initiatives that cater to the specific needs and interests of RSEs. Companies could also use the insights from this study to create more effective recruitment and retention strategies for RSEs, which could lead to increased revenue and competitiveness in the industry.

case_studies.title: Leveraging LLMs for Multi-File DSL Code Generation: An Industrial Case Study
case_studies.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) perform strongly on general-purpose code generation, yet their applicability to enterprise domain-specific languages (DSLs) remains underexplored, especially for repository-scale change generation spanning multiple files and folder structures from a single natural-language (NL) instruction. We report an industrial case study at BMW that adapts code-oriented LLMs to generate and modify project-root DSL artifacts for an Xtext-based DSL that drives downstream Java/TypeScript code generation. case_studies.summary: The problem addressed in this case study is the applicability of large language models (LLMs) to enterprise domain-specific languages (DSLs) for code generation. The AI approach involves adapting code-oriented LLMs to generate and modify project-root DSL artifacts for an Xtext-based DSL. The outcome is an end-to-end pipeline for dataset construction and multi-file task generation from a single natural-language instruction, as demonstrated in an industrial case study at BMW.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can develop similar pipelines for their own DSLs by leveraging code-oriented LLMs and constructing datasets tailored to their specific use cases. They can also experiment with adapting LLMs to generate code for multiple files and folder structures from a single natural-language instruction.
case_studies.monetisation: The monetisation potential of this approach lies in its ability to streamline code generation and modification for enterprises, reducing manual labor and increasing efficiency. A concrete business opportunity could be to develop a product or service that provides tailored LLM-based code generation solutions for companies using domain-specific languages.

case_studies.title: Characterizing Vision-Language-Action Models across XPUs: Constraints and Acceleration for On-Robot Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are promising for generalist robot control, but on-robot deployment is bottlenecked by real-time inference under tight cost and energy budgets. Most prior evaluations rely on desktop-grade GPUs, obscuring the trade-offs and opportunities offered by heterogeneous edge accelerators (GPUs/XPUs/NPUs). case_studies.summary: The problem of deploying Vision-Language-Action models on robots is bottlenecked by real-time inference under tight cost and energy budgets. To address this, the authors present a systematic analysis for low-cost VLA deployment via model-hardware co-characterization, evaluating model-hardware pairs under cost, energy, and time constraints. case_studies.summary: The problem of relying on cloud-based workflows for machine learning tasks is addressed by developing an on-device vision machine learning pipeline. The AI approach involves using a two-layer CNN with Adam optimization, trained and deployed on a microcontroller-class device. The outcome is a complete, end-to-end vision machine learning pipeline that can run in real-time on a low-cost device.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this approach by leveraging microcontroller-class devices to develop edge-based machine learning solutions, reducing reliance on cloud infrastructure. case_studies.abstract: Bridging the gap between embodied intelligence and embedded deployment remains a key challenge in intelligent robotic systems, where perception, reasoning, and planning must operate under strict constraints on computation, memory, energy, and real-time execution. In vision-language navigation (VLN), existing approaches often face a fundamental trade-off between strong reasoning capabilities and efficient deployment on real-world platforms. case_studies.summary: The problem of bridging the gap between embodied intelligence and embedded deployment in intelligent robotic systems is addressed through a vision-language navigation system. The AI approach involves hierarchical cognition and context-aware exploration to achieve both high efficiency and robust high-level reasoning. The outcome is a deployable embodied vision-language navigation system that can operate on real-world robotic platforms.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this concept, AI practitioners can focus on developing hierarchical cognitive models that balance strong reasoning capabilities with efficient deployment on real-world platforms. case_studies.title: Cortex 2.0: Grounding World Models in Real-World Industrial Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Industrial robotic manipulation demands reliable long-horizon execution across embodiments, tasks, and changing object distributions. While Vision-Language-Action models have demonstrated strong generalization, they remain fundamentally reactive. By optimizing the next action given the current observation without evaluating potential futures, they are brittle to the compounding failure modes of long-horizon tasks. case_studies.summary: Industrial robotic manipulation requires reliable long-horizon execution, but current Vision-Language-Action models are reactive and prone to failure. Cortex 2.0 addresses this by shifting to a plan-and-act approach, generating candidate future trajectories and scoring them for success and efficiency. This approach enables more robust and efficient execution of industrial robotic tasks.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can focus on developing models that generate and evaluate potential future trajectories, rather than just reacting to current observations. By incorporating planning and evaluation into their models, practitioners can create more robust and efficient AI systems for industrial robotic manipulation.
case_studies.monetisation: The Cortex 2.0 approach presents a clear business opportunity for companies developing industrial robotic systems, as it enables more efficient and reliable execution of tasks. By integrating this technology into their products, companies can differentiate themselves and attract customers seeking more robust and efficient industrial robotic solutions.

case_studies.summary: The generation of real-world evidence from large health record datasets is a manual process that requires significant expertise, limiting its scalability and efficiency. case_studies.title: AgentPulse: A Continuous Multi-Signal Framework for Evaluating AI Agents in Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Static benchmarks measure what AI agents can do at a fixed point in time but not how they are adopted, maintained, or experienced in deployment. case_studies.summary: The evaluation of AI agents is limited by static benchmarks that do not account for real-world deployment and user experience. The framework demonstrates its effectiveness through analyses of 50 agents across 10 workload categories, providing a more comprehensive understanding of AI agent performance and adoption.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this framework, AI practitioners can integrate AgentPulse into their development workflows to monitor and evaluate their AI agents' performance and adoption in real-time. case_studies.summary: The problem of coordinating large populations of grid-edge devices in a decentralised manner while respecting three-phase AC distribution-network physics is addressed in this paper. The outcome of this approach is a decentralised learning method that enables online decision-making without communication among agents.

case_studies.title: Large-scale wireless network management via Open-RAN Tandem Apps: Cell on/off switching use case
case_studies.abstract: With growing mobile-network complexity, management and optimization have become increasingly difficult. case_studies.summary: The growing complexity of mobile networks has made management and optimization increasingly difficult, with centralized algorithms facing high control-data overhead and distributed approaches often performing suboptimally. This work proposes Tandem Apps, a pair of tightly coupled optimization mechanisms running on both RAN Intelligent Controllers (RICs) in the O-RAN architecture, to achieve agile and low-complexity network management. The proposed approach enables hierarchical network-management schemes, but its practical implementation and outcome are still theoretical.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this concept, AI practitioners can explore the design of Tandem Apps through architectural and functional splitting to achieve agile and low-complexity network management. By leveraging the O-RAN architecture and RICs, practitioners can develop hierarchical network-management schemes that address the limitations of centralized and distributed approaches.

By developing and refining this concept, companies can create tailored products and services that address the growing need for efficient and scalable network management solutions.

case_studies.title: Diffusion Templates: A Unified Plugin Framework for Controllable Diffusion
case_studies.abstract: Controllable diffusion methods have substantially expanded the practical utility of diffusion models, but they are typically developed as isolated, backbone-specific systems with incompatible training pipelines, parameter formats, and runtime hooks. This fragmentation makes it difficult to reuse infrastructure across tasks, transfer capabilities across backbones, or compose multiple controls within a single generation pipeline. case_studies.summary: The problem of fragmentation in controllable diffusion methods is addressed by decoupling base-model inference from controllable capability injection. This framework allows for greater flexibility and reusability of infrastructure across tasks, enabling the composition of multiple controls within a single generation pipeline.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this framework by developing plugins for specific controllable diffusion methods, allowing for seamless integration with existing base models. By doing so, they can create more flexible and reusable generation pipelines, facilitating the transfer of capabilities across different backbone models.
case_studies.monetisation: The Diffusion Templates framework presents a concrete business opportunity for companies developing AI-powered generative models, as it enables the creation of more versatile and adaptable models. By licensing or integrating this framework, businesses can accelerate their development of controllable diffusion methods, providing a competitive edge in applications such as image and video generation, music synthesis, and text-to-speech systems.

case_studies.summary: The problem addressed in this study is the joint equidistribution of Hecke eigenvalues for cusp forms and elliptic curves over finite fields. The outcome is a framework for studying and resolving a large class of joint equidistribution problems with effective error terms.

case_studies.abstract: We study learning with Chain-of-Thought (CoT) supervision from multiple thinkers, all of whom provide correct but possibly systematically different solutions, e.g., step-by-step solutions to math problems written by different thinkers, or step-by-step execution traces of different programs solving the same problem. case_studies.summary: The problem addressed in this study is the difficulty of learning from Chain-of-Thought (CoT) supervision from multiple thinkers, which can provide correct but systematically different solutions. The AI approach involves learning with CoT supervision from multiple thinkers, analyzing the impact of cryptographic assumptions on the learning process. The outcome of this study establishes the hardness of learning from CoT supervision under certain assumptions, providing insights into the limitations of CoT learning.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply the findings of this study, AI practitioners should consider the potential biases and limitations of CoT supervision from multiple thinkers when designing and training AI models. This can involve carefully evaluating the consistency and quality of the supervision data to ensure that the model learns effectively and generalizes well to new situations.

case_studies.title: Green Shielding: A User-Centric Approach Towards Trustworthy AI
case_studies.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed, yet their outputs can be highly sensitive to routine, non-adversarial variation in how users phrase queries, a gap not well addressed by existing red-teaming efforts. case_studies.summary: The problem addressed in this study is the sensitivity of large language models to variations in user input, which can lead to inconsistent and potentially misleading results. The outcome of this approach is the development of evidence-backed deployment guidance for building trustworthy AI models.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply the lessons from this study, AI practitioners can prioritize the development of user-centric evaluation metrics that capture realistic variations in user input, rather than relying on traditional red-teaming efforts. case_studies.title: Benchmarking Source-Sensitive Reasoning in Turkish: Humans and LLMs under Evidential Trust Manipulation

case_studies.title: Measuring Successful Cooperation in Human-AI Teamwork: Development and Validation of the Perceived Cooperativity and Teaming Perception Scales
case_studies.abstract: As human-AI cooperation becomes increasingly prevalent, reliable instruments for assessing the subjective quality of cooperative human-AI interaction are needed. case_studies.summary: The problem of measuring successful cooperation in human-AI teamwork is addressed through the development of two scales: the Perceived Cooperativity Scale and the Teaming Perception Scale.
